questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: When a block of mass $M$ is suspended by a long wire of length $L$, the length of the wire becomes $(L + l)$. The elastic potential energy stored in the extended wire is:
questions.solution_text: Elastic potential energy stored = $\frac{1}{2} \times$ restoring force $\times$ extension $= \frac{1}{2} \times Mg \times l = \frac{1}{2}Mgl$. Note: Work done by gravity is $Mgl$ but only half is stored as elastic PE.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A mass $m$ is attached to a thin wire and whirled in a vertical circle. The wire is most likely to break when:

options.text: the mass is at the highest point
the mass is at the lowest point
inclined at an angle of $60°$ from vertical

questions.solution_text: Tension at any point: $T - mg\cos\theta = \frac{mv^2}{r}$. At lowest point $\theta = 180°$, so $T = \frac{mv^2}{r} + mg$. This is maximum, so wire most likely breaks at lowest point.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Radius of circular path in magnetic field
questions.question_text: Ionized hydrogen atoms and $\alpha$-particles with same momenta enter perpendicular to a constant magnetic field $B$. The ratio of their radii of their paths $r_H : r_\alpha$ will be:
questions.solution_text: Radius $r = \frac{p}{qB}$. For same momentum $p$: $r_H = \frac{p}{eB}$, $r_\alpha = \frac{p}{2eB}$ (since $\alpha$ has charge $2e$). So $\frac{r_H}{r_\alpha} = \frac{2eB}{eB} = 2:1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Body $A$ of mass $4m$ moving with speed $u$ collides with another body $B$ of mass $2m$, at rest. The collision is head on and elastic in nature. After the collision the fraction of energy lost by the colliding body $A$ is:
questions.solution_text: Fractional loss of KE of colliding body $= \frac{4m_1 m_2}{(m_1+m_2)^2} = \frac{4 \times 4m \times 2m}{(4m+2m)^2} = \frac{32m^2}{36m^2} = \frac{8}{9}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a double slit experiment, when light of wavelength $400\,nm$ was used, the angular width of the first minima formed on a screen placed $1\,m$ away was found to be $0.2°$. What will be the angular width of the first minima if the entire experimental apparatus is immersed in water? ($\mu_{water} = 4/3$)
questions.solution_text: Angular fringe width $\propto \lambda$. In water, $\lambda_w = \frac{\lambda}{\mu} = \frac{\lambda}{4/3}$. So new angular width $= 0.2 \times \frac{3}{4} = 0.15°$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In which of the following devices, the eddy current effect is not used?
questions.solution_text: Electric heater does not involve eddy currents. It uses Joule's heating effect ($Q = I^2Rt$). Induction furnace, magnetic braking, and electromagnets all use eddy current effects.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A soap bubble, having radius of $1\,mm$, is blown from a detergent solution having a surface tension of $2.5 \times 10^{-2}\,N/m$. The pressure inside the bubble equals at a point $Z_0$ below the free surface of water in a container. Taking $g = 10\,m/s^2$, density of water $= 10^3\,kg/m^3$, the value of $Z_0$ is:
questions.solution_text: Excess pressure in soap bubble $= \frac{4T}{R} = \frac{4 \times 2.5 \times 10^{-2}}{1 \times 10^{-3}} = 100\,Pa$. This equals $\rho g Z_0$, so $Z_0 = \frac{100}{10^3 \times 10} = 0.01\,m = 1\,cm$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which colour of the light has the longest wavelength?
questions.solution_text: In the visible spectrum, VIBGYOR order: Violet has shortest wavelength (~380nm) and Red has the longest wavelength (~700nm).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Systems of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Systems of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question_text: A disc of radius $2\,m$ and mass $100\,kg$ rolls on a horizontal floor. Its centre of mass has speed of $20\,cm/s$. How much work is needed to stop it?
questions.solution_text: Total KE of rolling disc $= \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2 = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{mr^2}{2} \cdot \frac{v^2}{r^2} = \frac{3}{4}mv^2 = \frac{3}{4} \times 100 \times (0.2)^2 = \frac{3}{4} \times 4 = 3\,J$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The displacement of a particle executing simple harmonic motion is given by $y = A_0 + A\sin\omega t + B\cos\omega t$. Then the amplitude of its oscillation is given by:
questions.solution_text: $y' = y - A_0 = A\sin\omega t + B\cos\omega t$ represents SHM. Resultant amplitude $= \sqrt{A^2 + B^2 + 2AB\cos90°} = \sqrt{A^2 + B^2}$. $A_0$ is just a shift in mean position, not part of amplitude.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two similar thin equi-convex lenses, of focal length $f$ each, are kept coaxially in contact with each other such that the focal length of the combination is $F_1$. When the space between the two lenses is filled with glycerine (which has the same refractive index $\mu = 1.5$ as that of glass) then the equivalent focal length is $F_2$. The ratio $F_1 : F_2$ will be:
questions.solution_text: Without glycerine: $\frac{1}{F_1} = \frac{1}{f} + \frac{1}{f} = \frac{2}{f}$, so $F_1 = f/2$. With glycerine ($\mu_{glycerine} = \mu_{glass} = 1.5$), glycerine acts as a diverging lens of focal length $-f$. $\frac{1}{F_2} = \frac{1}{f} + \frac{1}{-f} + \frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{f}$, so $F_2 = f$. Thus $F_1:F_2 = f/2 : f = 1:2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Effect of temperature on gas properties
questions.question_text: Increase in temperature of a gas filled in a container would lead to:
questions.solution_text: For an ideal gas, internal energy $U = \frac{f}{2}nRT$. Increase in temperature increases the average kinetic energy of gas molecules. Mass doesn't change, pressure increases (not decreases), and intermolecular distance increases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated electron
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question_text: An electron is accelerated through a potential difference of $10,000\,V$. Its de Broglie wavelength is nearly: ($m_e = 9 \times 10^{-31}\,kg$)
questions.solution_text: de Broglie wavelength $\lambda = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}\,\text{Å} = \frac{12.27}{\sqrt{10000}} = \frac{12.27}{100} = 0.1227\,\text{Å} = 12.27 \times 10^{-12}\,m \approx 12.2 \times 10^{-12}\,m$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A copper rod of $88\,cm$ and an aluminium rod of unknown length have their increase in length independent of increase in temperature. The length of aluminium rod is: ($\alpha_{Cu} = 1.7 \times 10^{-5}\,K^{-1}$ and $\alpha_{Al} = 2.2 \times 10^{-5}\,K^{-1}$)
questions.solution_text: For equal expansion: $\alpha_{Cu} L_{Cu} = \alpha_{Al} L_{Al}$. So $L_{Al} = \frac{\alpha_{Cu}}{\alpha_{Al}} \times L_{Cu} = \frac{1.7 \times 10^{-5}}{2.2 \times 10^{-5}} \times 88 = \frac{1.7}{2.2} \times 88 = 68\,cm$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Pick the wrong answer in the context with rainbow.

options.text: When the light rays undergo two internal reflections in a water drop, a secondary rainbow is formed
The order of colours is reversed in the secondary rainbow
An observer can see a rainbow when his front is towards the sun
Rainbow is a combined effect of dispersion, refraction and reflection of sunlight

questions.solution_text: Rainbow cannot be observed when the observer faces towards the sun. The observer must have the sun behind them and face the water droplets (rain) in front to see a rainbow.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A body weighs $200\,N$ on the surface of the earth. How much will it weigh half way down to the centre of the earth?
questions.solution_text: $g_d = g\left(1 - \frac{d}{R}\right)$. At $d = R/2$: $g_d = g\left(1 - \frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{g}{2}$. Weight $= mg_d = 200 \times \frac{1}{2} = 100\,N$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Power consumption with bulbs in series and parallel
questions.question_text: Six similar bulbs are connected as shown in the figure with a DC source of emf $E$ and zero internal resistance. The ratio of power consumption by the bulbs when (i) all are glowing and (ii) in the situation when two from section A and one from section B are glowing, will be:
questions.solution_text: Case (i) all glowing: $R_{eq} = \frac{2R}{3}$, $P_i = \frac{3E^2}{2R}$. Case (ii) 2 from A + 1 from B: $R_{eq} = \frac{3R}{2}$, $P_f = \frac{2E^2}{3R}$. Ratio $P_i:P_f = \frac{3E^2}{2R} : \frac{2E^2}{3R} = 9:4$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: For a p-type semiconductor, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Electrons are the majority carriers and trivalent atoms are the dopants.
Holes are the majority carriers and trivalent atoms are the dopants.
Holes are the majority carriers and pentavalent atoms are the dopants.
Electrons are the majority carriers and pentavalent atoms are the dopants.

questions.solution_text: In p-type semiconductor, intrinsic semiconductor is doped with trivalent impurities (like B, Al, In). This creates deficiency of valence electrons called holes which are the majority charge carriers.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Average velocity of a particle executing SHM in one complete vibration is:
questions.solution_text: In one complete vibration, the particle returns to its initial position, so net displacement = 0. Average velocity $= \frac{\text{displacement}}{\text{time}} = \frac{0}{T} = 0$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The unit of thermal conductivity is:
questions.solution_text: From $\frac{dH}{dt} = KA\frac{\Delta T}{l}$, $K = \frac{dH/dt \cdot l}{A \cdot \Delta T}$. Units: $\frac{W \cdot m}{m^2 \cdot K} = W\,m^{-1}\,K^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Systems of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Systems of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question_text: A solid cylinder of mass $2\,kg$ and radius $4\,cm$ rotating about its axis at the rate of $3\,rpm$. The torque required to stop after $2$ revolutions is:
questions.solution_text: $I = \frac{1}{2}mr^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times (4\times10^{-2})^2 = 1.6\times10^{-3}\,kg\,m^2$. $\omega_i = 3\,rpm = \frac{3 \times 2\pi}{60} = \frac{\pi}{10}\,rad/s$. $\theta = 2 \times 2\pi = 4\pi\,rad$. By work-energy: $\tau \cdot \theta = \frac{1}{2}I\omega_i^2$, so $\tau = \frac{I\omega_i^2}{2\theta} = \frac{1.6\times10^{-3} \times (\pi/10)^2}{8\pi} \approx 2\times10^{-6}\,N\,m$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Which of the following acts as a circuit protecting device?
questions.solution_text: Fuse wire has a low melting point. When excess current flows, the heat produced ($Q = I^2Rt$) melts it, breaking the circuit and protecting it from damage.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In the circuits shown below, the readings of voltmeters and the ammeters will be (Circuit 1: Voltmeter $V_1$ and Ammeter $A_1$ with $10\,V$ source and $10\,\Omega$ resistor. Circuit 2: Voltmeter $V_2$ and Ammeter $A_2$ with $10\,V$ source and two $10\,\Omega$ resistors):
questions.solution_text: For ideal voltmeter: $R = \infty$; for ideal ammeter: $R = 0$. In both circuits $V = 10\,V$ (voltmeter reads full source voltage) and $i = 10/10 = 1\,A$ (ammeter reads current through $10\,\Omega$). So $V_1 = V_2 = 10\,V$ and $i_1 = i_2 = 1\,A$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Electric field of hollow metal sphere
questions.question_text: A hollow metal sphere of radius $R$ is uniformly charged. The electric field due to the sphere at a distance $r$ from the centre:

options.text: Increases as $r$ increases for $r < R$ and for $r > R$
Zero as $r$ increases for $r < R$, decreases as $r$ increases for $r > R$
Zero as $r$ increases for $r < R$, increases as $r$ increases for $r > R$
Decreases as $r$ increases for $r < R$ and for $r > R$

questions.solution_text: By Gauss's law: For $r < R$ (inside): $q_{enclosed} = 0$, so $E = 0$. For $r > R$ (outside): $E = \frac{Q}{4\pi\epsilon_0 r^2} \propto \frac{1}{r^2}$, which decreases as $r$ increases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: At a point A on the earth's surface the angle of dip, $\delta = +25°$. At a point B on the earth's surface the angle of dip, $\delta = -25°$. We can interpret that:

options.text: A and B are both located in the northern hemisphere.
A is located in the southern hemisphere and B is located in the northern hemisphere.
A is located in the northern hemisphere and B is located in the southern hemisphere.
A and B are both located in the southern hemisphere.

questions.solution_text: Dip angle is positive in the northern hemisphere (field dips toward north) and negative in the southern hemisphere (field dips toward south). So A (+25°) is in the northern hemisphere and B (−25°) is in the southern hemisphere.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: KE and PE of electron in orbit
questions.question_text: The total energy of an electron in an atom in an orbit is $-3.4\,eV$. Its kinetic and potential energies are, respectively:
questions.solution_text: In Bohr's model: $KE = -E_{total} = -(-3.4) = 3.4\,eV$ (always positive). $PE = 2 \times E_{total} = 2 \times (-3.4) = -6.8\,eV$. Relation: $E_{total} = KE + PE = 3.4 + (-6.8) = -3.4\,eV$. ✓

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In total internal reflection when the angle of incidence is equal to the critical angle for the pair of media in contact, what will be angle of refraction?
questions.solution_text: At the critical angle, the refracted ray grazes along the interface between the two media. Therefore, the angle of refraction is $90°$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The work done to raise a mass $m$ from the surface of the earth to a height $h$, which is equal to the radius of the earth, is:
questions.solution_text: $W = U_f - U_i = \frac{-GMm}{2R} - \frac{-GMm}{R} = \frac{GMm}{2R} = \frac{gR^2 m}{2R} = \frac{mgR}{2}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: When an object is shot from the bottom of a long smooth inclined plane kept at an angle $60°$ with horizontal, it can travel a distance $x_1$ along the plane. But when the inclination is decreased to $30°$ and the same object is shot with the same velocity, it can travel $x_2$ distance. Then $x_1 : x_2$ will be:
questions.solution_text: Stopping distance $x = \frac{u^2}{2g\sin\theta}$. So $\frac{x_1}{x_2} = \frac{\sin30°}{\sin60°} = \frac{1/2}{\sqrt{3}/2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$. Thus $x_1:x_2 = 1:\sqrt{3}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: $\alpha$-particle consists of:
questions.solution_text: An $\alpha$-particle is the nucleus of a Helium atom ($^4_2He$), which contains 2 protons and 2 neutrons. It has no electrons.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The speed of a swimmer in still water is $20\,m/s$. The speed of river water is $10\,m/s$ and is flowing due east. If he is standing on the south bank and wishes to cross the river along the shortest path, the angle at which he should make his strokes w.r.t. north is given by:
questions.solution_text: For shortest path, the resultant velocity must be perpendicular to river (due north). $\sin\theta = \frac{V_{river}}{V_{swimmer}} = \frac{10}{20} = \frac{1}{2}$, so $\theta = 30°$ west of north.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A particle moving with velocity $\vec{V}$ is acted by three forces shown by the vector triangle PQR. The velocity of the particle will:

options.text: Change according to the smallest force $\vec{QR}$

questions.solution_text: When three forces form a closed vector triangle (in the same order), their vector sum is zero. So $\vec{F}_{net} = 0$, which means $m\frac{d\vec{v}}{dt} = 0$, and hence velocity remains constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two particles A and B are moving in uniform circular motion in concentric circles of radii $r_A$ and $r_B$ with speed $v_A$ and $v_B$ respectively. Their time period of rotation is the same. The ratio of angular speed of A to that of B will be:
questions.solution_text: $\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T}$. Since $T_A = T_B$, we have $\omega_A = \omega_B$, so the ratio $\omega_A : \omega_B = 1:1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Minimum angular velocity for block on cylinder wall
questions.question_text: A block of mass $10\,kg$ is in contact against the inner wall of a hollow cylindrical drum of radius $1\,m$. The coefficient of friction between the block and the inner wall of the cylinder is $0.1$. The minimum angular velocity needed for the cylinder to keep the block stationary when the cylinder is vertical and rotating about its axis, will be: ($g = 10\,m/s^2$)
questions.solution_text: For equilibrium: friction $f = mg$ and normal force $N = mr\omega^2$. At minimum: $\mu N = mg \Rightarrow \mu mr\omega^2 = mg \Rightarrow \omega = \sqrt{\frac{g}{\mu r}} = \sqrt{\frac{10}{0.1 \times 1}} = \sqrt{100} = 10\,rad/s$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Field due to infinite line charges
questions.question_text: Two parallel infinite line charges with linear charge densities $+\lambda\,C/m$ and $-\lambda\,C/m$ are placed at a distance of $2R$ in free space. What is the electric field mid-way between the two line charges?
questions.solution_text: Field due to $+\lambda$ at midpoint: $E_1 = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi\epsilon_0 R}$ (directed away). Field due to $-\lambda$: $E_2 = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi\epsilon_0 R}$ (directed toward $-\lambda$, same direction as $E_1$). Total $E = E_1 + E_2 = \frac{\lambda}{\pi\epsilon_0 R}\,N/C$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two point charges A and B, having charges $+Q$ and $-Q$ respectively, are placed at certain distance apart and force acting between them is $F$. If $25\%$ charge of A is transferred to B, then force between the charges becomes:
questions.solution_text: Initial: $F = \frac{kQ^2}{r^2}$. After transfer: $q_A = Q - \frac{Q}{4} = \frac{3Q}{4}$, $q_B = -Q + \frac{Q}{4} = -\frac{3Q}{4}$. New force $F_1 = \frac{k \cdot \frac{3Q}{4} \cdot \frac{3Q}{4}}{r^2} = \frac{9kQ^2}{16r^2} = \frac{9F}{16}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Rate of flow through orifice (Torricelli's theorem)
questions.question_text: A small hole of area of cross-section $2\,mm^2$ is present near the bottom of a fully filled open tank of height $2\,m$. Taking $g = 10\,m/s^2$, the rate of flow of water through the open hole would be nearly:
questions.solution_text: By Torricelli's theorem: $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 2} = \sqrt{40}\,m/s$. Rate of flow $Q = Av = 2 \times 10^{-6} \times \sqrt{40} = 2 \times 10^{-6} \times 6.32 \approx 12.6 \times 10^{-6}\,m^3/s$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The correct Boolean operation represented by the circuit diagram drawn is:
questions.solution_text: From the truth table in the figure: output is 0 only when both A=1 and B=1, and 1 otherwise. This matches the NAND gate truth table: $Y = \overline{A \cdot B}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In which of the following processes, heat is neither absorbed nor released by a system?
questions.solution_text: In an adiabatic process, $Q = 0$, i.e., no heat exchange takes place between the system and surroundings. By first law: $\Delta U = -W$ (work done at expense of internal energy).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A $800$ turn coil of effective area $0.05\,m^2$ is kept perpendicular to a magnetic field $5 \times 10^{-5}\,T$. When the plane of the coil is rotated by $90°$ around any of its coplanar axis in $0.1\,s$, the emf induced in the coil will be:
questions.solution_text: $\Delta\Phi = NBA(\cos90° - \cos0°) = -NBA = -800 \times 5\times10^{-5} \times 0.05 = -2\times10^{-3}\,Wb$. $e = -\frac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t} = \frac{2\times10^{-3}}{0.1} = 0.02\,V$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The radius of circle, the period of revolution, initial position and sense of revolution are indicated in the figure (radius $= 3\,m$, $T = 4\,s$, particle starts at maximum positive y). y-projection of the radius vector of rotating particle P is:
questions.solution_text: At $t=0$, particle is at maximum y, so cosine function. $\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T} = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\,rad/s$. Amplitude $= 3\,m$. So $y(t) = 3\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right)$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Conduction and displacement current in capacitor
questions.question_text: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance $20\,\mu F$ is being charged by a voltage source whose potential is changing at the rate of $3\,V/s$. The conduction current through the connecting wires, and the displacement current through the plates of the capacitor, would be, respectively:
questions.solution_text: Conduction current $i_c = C\frac{dV}{dt} = 20\times10^{-6} \times 3 = 60\,\mu A$. By Maxwell's law, displacement current $i_d = i_c = 60\,\mu A$. Both are equal and continuous.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Maximum percentage error in compound expression
questions.question_text: In an experiment, the percentage of error occurred in the measurement of physical quantities $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ are $1\%$, $2\%$, $3\%$ and $4\%$ respectively. Then the maximum percentage of error in the measurement $X$, where $X = \frac{A^{1/2}B^2}{C^{1/3}D^3}$, will be:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Magnetic field inside and outside a cylindrical conductor
questions.question_text: A cylindrical conductor of radius $R$ is carrying a constant current. The plot of the magnitude of the magnetic field $B$ with the distance $d$ from the centre of the conductor is correctly represented by the figure:

options.text: Graph showing B increasing for all d
Graph showing B decreasing for all d
Graph showing B increasing linearly for $d<R$ and decreasing hyperbolically for $d>R$
Graph showing B constant for $d<R$ and decreasing for $d>R$

questions.solution_text: Inside ($d<R$): $B = \frac{\mu_0 i}{2\pi R^2}d$ (linear, increases with d). At surface ($d=R$): $B_{max} = \frac{\mu_0 i}{2\pi R}$. Outside ($d>R$): $B = \frac{\mu_0 i}{2\pi d}$ (hyperbolic, decreases with d).

questions.solution_text: Structure: H–C–C=C–C≡C–H with H's on C1 and C2. Number of σ bonds = 10 and number of π bonds = 3 (one from double bond, two from triple bond).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The structure of intermediate A in the following reaction is: $\text{CH(CH}_3)_2 \xrightarrow{O_2} A \xrightarrow{H^+/H_2O} OH + H_3C-CO-CH_3$
questions.solution_text: Cumene (isopropylbenzene) reacts with O2 to form cumene hydroperoxide (H3C-C(CH3)-O-O-H attached to benzene ring) as intermediate A. This on acid hydrolysis gives phenol and acetone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The correct structure of tribromooctaoxide is:

options.text: $O=Br-Br-Br=O$ with 3 oxygens on each terminal Br and 2 on middle Br
Structure with negative charges on oxygens

questions.solution_text: Tribromooctaoxide (Br3O8) has the correct structure O=Br(-O)2-Br(-O)2-Br(=O)(-O) — each Br in +5 oxidation state, with Br-Br bonds connecting the three bromine atoms and oxide groups attached.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 4d, 5p, 5f and 6p orbitals are arranged in the order of decreasing energy. The correct option is:
questions.solution_text: (n+l) values: 4d = 6, 5p = 6, 5f = 8, 6p = 7. Higher (n+l) = higher energy. For same (n+l), higher n = higher energy. So 5f(8) > 6p(7) > 5p(6) > 4d(6) [5p has higher n than 4d].

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following reactions are disproportionation reactions? (a) $2Cu^+ \to Cu^0 + Cu^{2+}$ (b) $MnO_4^- + 4H^+ \to 2MnO_2 + MnO_4^{2-} + 2H_2O$ (c) $2KMnO_4 \to K_2MnO_4 + MnO_2 + O_2$ (d) $MnO_4^- + 3Mn^{2+} + 2H_2O \to 5MnO_2 + 4H^+$
questions.solution_text: In disproportionation, same element is simultaneously oxidised and reduced. (a) Cu+1 → Cu0 (reduced) + Cu+2 (oxidised): disproportionation. (b) Mn+7 → Mn+4 and Mn+6: disproportionation. (c) and (d) are not disproportionation reactions.

questions.question_text: Under isothermal condition, a gas at 300 K expands from 0.1 L to 0.25 L against a constant external pressure of 2 bar. The work done by the gas is (Given that 1 L bar = 100 J):

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Among the following, the one that is not a greenhouse gas is:
questions.solution_text: SO2 is not a greenhouse gas. Greenhouse gases include CO2, CH4, N2O, O3, and CFCs. SO2 causes acid rain but does not trap infrared radiation like greenhouse gases do.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Standard Gibbs energy from cell EMF
questions.question_text: For the cell reaction $2Fe^{3+}(aq) + 2I^-(aq) \to 2Fe^{2+}(aq) + I_2(aq)$, $E^\circ_{cell} = 0.24\,V$ at 298 K. The standard Gibbs energy $\Delta_r G^\circ$ is: [F = 96500 C mol$^{-1}$]
questions.solution_text: $\Delta_r G^\circ = -nFE^\circ_{cell} = -2 \times 96500 \times 0.24 = -46320\,J\,mol^{-1} = -46.32\,kJ\,mol^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Enzymes that utilize ATP in phosphate transfer require an alkaline earth metal (M) as the cofactor. M is:
questions.solution_text: All enzymes that utilize ATP in phosphate transfer require magnesium (Mg) as the cofactor. Mg2+ stabilizes the polyphosphate chain of ATP.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Partial hydrogenation to give cis alkene
questions.question_text: The most suitable reagent for conversion of an alkyne to cis-2-butene is:
questions.solution_text: Lindlar's catalyst (H2, Pd/C, quinoline) reduces alkynes to cis-alkenes (syn addition of H2). Na/liquid NH3 gives trans-alkene (Birch reduction).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which is the correct thermal stability order for H2E (E = O, S, Se, Te and Po)?
questions.solution_text: On going down the group, H–E bond energy decreases so thermal stability decreases. H2O has the highest stability due to strong O–H bond. Correct order: H2Po < H2Te < H2Se < H2S < H2O.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following is an incorrect statement?

options.text: GeX4 (X = F, Cl, Br, I) is more stable than GeX2

questions.solution_text: PbF4 is ionic in nature (not covalent) because Pb4+ is a large ion and F– is small, leading to ionic character. SnF4 is also ionic. So statement (1) is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Match the industrial process with product
questions.question_text: Match the following: (a) Pure nitrogen (b) Haber process (c) Contact process (d) Deacon's process with (i) Chlorine (ii) Sulphuric acid (iii) Ammonia (iv) Sodium azide or Barium azide
questions.solution_text: Pure nitrogen: Sodium/Barium azide. Haber process: Ammonia. Contact process: Sulphuric acid. Deacon's process: Chlorine (oxidation of HCl).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following diatomic molecular species has only $\pi$ bonds according to Molecular Orbital Theory?
questions.solution_text: MO configuration of C2: $\sigma1s^2, \sigma^*1s^2, \sigma2s^2, \sigma^*2s^2, \pi2p_x^2, \pi2p_y^2$. The bonding is due to two π bonds only (the σ and σ* cancel each other), so C2 has only π bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: First ionisation enthalpy order for period 2
questions.question_text: For the second period elements the correct increasing order of first ionisation enthalpy is:

options.text: $Li < Be < B < C < N < O < F < Ne$
$Li < B < Be < C < O < N < F < Ne$
$Li < B < Be < C < N < O < F < Ne$
$Li < Be < B < C < O < N < F < Ne$

questions.solution_text: Be (2s2) and N (2p3) have extra stability due to filled and half-filled subshells respectively. So IE of Be > B and IE of N > O. Correct order: Li < B < Be < C < O < N < F < Ne.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The biodegradable polymer is:
questions.solution_text: Nylon-2-Nylon 6 is a biodegradable polymer. It is a copolymer of glycine (Nylon-2) and amino caproic acid (Nylon-6). Its amide bonds can be broken by microorganisms.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Ksp from pH of saturated solution
questions.question_text: pH of a saturated solution of Ca(OH)2 is 9. The solubility product (Ksp) of Ca(OH)2 is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: If the rate constant for a first order reaction is k, the time (t) required for the completion of 99% of the reaction is given by:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The non-essential amino acid among the following is:
questions.solution_text: Alanine is a non-essential amino acid (can be synthesized by the body). Valine, Leucine and Lysine are essential amino acids that must be obtained from the diet.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Among the following, the reaction that proceeds through an electrophilic substitution is:

options.text: Benzene + Cl2 with AlCl3 → chlorobenzene + HCl
Benzene + Cl2 under UV light → benzene hexachloride

questions.solution_text: Chlorination of benzene with Cl2/AlCl3 proceeds via electrophilic aromatic substitution (EAS). AlCl3 generates Cl+ electrophile. Options 1 is nucleophilic substitution, 3 is free radical, 4 is nucleophilic substitution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The mixture that forms maximum boiling azeotrope is:
questions.solution_text: Solutions showing negative deviation from Raoult's law form maximum boiling azeotrope. Water + HNO3 shows strong negative deviation (H-bonding between unlike molecules) and forms a maximum boiling azeotrope.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Relationship between rates of reactants and products
questions.question_text: For the chemical reaction $N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \to 2NH_3(g)$, the correct option is:
questions.solution_text: Rate = $-\frac{d[N_2]}{dt} = -\frac{1}{3}\frac{d[H_2]}{dt} = \frac{1}{2}\frac{d[NH_3]}{dt}$. So $-\frac{d[N_2]}{dt} = \frac{1}{2}\frac{d[NH_3]}{dt}$ is correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The number of moles of hydrogen molecules required to produce 20 moles of ammonia through Haber's process is:
questions.solution_text: $N_2 + 3H_2 \to 2NH_3$. For 20 moles of NH3: moles of H2 = $\frac{3}{2} \times 20 = 30$ moles.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The compound that is most difficult to protonate is:
questions.solution_text: In phenol, the lone pair on oxygen is in conjugation with the benzene ring (resonance), making it less available for protonation. Hence phenol is the most difficult to protonate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For an ideal solution, the correct option is:
questions.solution_text: For ideal solutions: ΔmixH = 0, ΔmixV = 0, ΔmixS > 0, ΔmixG < 0. The enthalpy of mixing is zero because interactions between unlike molecules equal those between like molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Conjugate bases for Brønsted acids H2O and HF are:
questions.solution_text: Conjugate base is formed by removal of H+. H2O loses H+ → OH–. HF loses H+ → F–. So conjugate bases are OH– and F– respectively.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which mixture of the solutions will lead to the formation of negatively charged colloidal [AgI]I$^-$ sol?

options.text: 50 mL of 1 M AgNO3 + 50 mL of 1.5 M KI
50 mL of 1 M AgNO3 + 50 mL of 2 M KI
50 mL of 2 M AgNO3 + 50 mL of 1.5 M KI
50 mL of 0.1 M AgNO3 + 50 mL of 0.1 M KI

questions.solution_text: For negatively charged AgI sol, excess I– ions must be present (adsorbed on AgI surface). Option 2: mmol KI = 100, mmol AgNO3 = 50. Excess KI → I– ions adsorbed → negatively charged sol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Among the following, the narrow spectrum antibiotic is:
questions.solution_text: Penicillin G is a narrow spectrum antibiotic effective mainly against Gram-positive bacteria. Ampicillin, Amoxycillin and Chloramphenicol are broad spectrum antibiotics.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An alkene 'A' on reaction with O3 and Zn–H2O gives propanone and ethanal in equimolar ratio. Addition of HCl to alkene 'A' gives 'B' as the major product. The structure of product 'B' is:
questions.solution_text: Ozonolysis gives propanone (CH3COCH3) + ethanal (CH3CHO), so alkene A is CH3-C(CH3)=CH-CH3 (2-methylbut-2-ene). HCl addition (Markovnikov) gives Cl at more substituted carbon: CH3-CH2-C(CH3)2-Cl.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: What is the correct electronic configuration of the central atom in K4[Fe(CN)6] based on crystal field theory?
questions.solution_text: Fe2+ in K4[Fe(CN)6]: 3d6. CN– is a strong field ligand causing pairing. All 6 electrons pair in t2g: configuration is $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$ (low spin complex).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Identify the incorrect statement related to PCl5 from the following:

options.text: Three equatorial P–Cl bonds make an angle of 120° with each other
Two axial P–Cl bonds make an angle of 180° with each other
Axial P–Cl bonds are longer than equatorial P–Cl bonds

questions.solution_text: PCl5 is reactive due to weaker and longer axial P–Cl bonds (240 pm vs 202 pm equatorial). Statements 1, 2, and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which will make a basic buffer?

options.text: 50 mL of 0.1 M NaOH + 25 mL of 0.1 M CH3COOH
100 mL of 0.1 M CH3COOH + 100 mL of 0.1 M NaOH
100 mL of 0.1 M HCl + 200 mL of 0.1 M NH4OH
100 mL of 0.1 M HCl + 100 mL of 0.1 M NaOH

questions.solution_text: Option 3: HCl (10 mmol) + NH4OH (20 mmol) → NH4Cl (10 mmol) + excess NH4OH (10 mmol). Mixture of weak base NH4OH + its salt NH4Cl = basic buffer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The major product of the following reaction is: Phthalic acid + NH3 with strong heating →
questions.solution_text: Phthalic acid + NH3 → ammonium salt → monoamide → on strong heating, loses water to form phthalimide (cyclic imide with N-H between two C=O groups).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Match the Xenon compounds in Column-I with its structure in Column-II: (a) XeF4 (i) Pyramidal (b) XeF6 (ii) Square planar (c) XeOF4 (iii) Distorted octahedral (d) XeO3 (iv) Square pyramidal
questions.solution_text: XeF4: 2 lone pairs → square planar. XeF6: 1 lone pair → distorted octahedral. XeOF4: 1 lone pair → square pyramidal. XeO3: 1 lone pair → pyramidal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.ncert_chapter_name: The d and f Block Elements
questions.question_text: The manganate and permanganate ions are tetrahedral, due to:

options.text: The π-bonding involves overlap of p-orbitals of oxygen with d-orbitals of manganese
The π-bonding involves overlap of p-orbitals of oxygen with p-orbitals of manganese
The π-bonding involves overlap of d-orbitals of oxygen with d-orbitals of manganese

questions.solution_text: In manganate (MnO42–) and permanganate (MnO4–), the π-bonding is of d-p type: p-orbitals of oxygen overlap with d-orbitals of manganese. This π-bonding contributes to tetrahedral geometry.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following species is not stable?
questions.solution_text: [SiCl6]2– does not exist/is not stable because six large Cl– ions cannot be accommodated around the small Si4+ ion due to size limitations. [SiF6]2– is stable as F– is small.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For a cell involving one electron $E^\circ_{cell} = 0.59\,V$ at 298 K, the equilibrium constant for the cell reaction is: (Given $\frac{2.303RT}{F} = 0.059\,V$ at T = 298 K)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following is an amphoteric hydroxide?
questions.solution_text: Be(OH)2 is amphoteric — reacts with acids (Be(OH)2 + 2HCl → BeCl2 + 2H2O) and with bases (Be(OH)2 + 2NaOH → Na2[Be(OH)4]). This is due to the small size and high charge density of Be2+.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A gas at 350 K and 15 bar has molar volume 20 percent smaller than that for an ideal gas under the same conditions. The correct option about the gas and its compressibility factor (Z) is:

options.text: Z > 1 and attractive forces are dominant
Z > 1 and repulsive forces are dominant
Z < 1 and attractive forces are dominant
Z < 1 and repulsive forces are dominant

questions.solution_text: Z = Vreal/Videal. Since Vreal is 20% smaller than Videal, Z < 1. When Z < 1, attractive forces between molecules dominate, causing the gas to occupy less volume than ideal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Formula from hcp lattice and octahedral voids
questions.question_text: A compound is formed by cation C and anion A. The anions form hexagonal close packed (hcp) lattice and the cations occupy 75% of octahedral voids. The formula of the compound is:
questions.solution_text: In hcp, per unit cell: A = 6, octahedral voids = 6. Cations in 75% OV = 6 × 0.75 = 4.5 = 9/2. Ratio C:A = 9/2 : 6 = 9:12 = 3:4. Formula: C3A4.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In which case is change in entropy negative?

options.text: Expansion of a gas at constant temperature

questions.solution_text: $2H(g) \to H_2(g)$: two moles of gas → one mole of gas. Δng < 0, so disorder decreases → ΔS < 0 (negative). All other options involve increase in disorder.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following series of transitions in the spectrum of hydrogen atom fall in visible region?
questions.solution_text: Balmer series (transitions to n=2) falls in visible region (400–700 nm). Lyman series: UV region. Paschen, Brackett: IR region.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The method used to remove temporary hardness of water is:
questions.solution_text: Clark's method removes temporary hardness by adding slaked lime Ca(OH)2 which converts soluble bicarbonates of Ca and Mg to insoluble carbonates/hydroxides that precipitate out.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.ncert_chapter_name: The d and f Block Elements
questions.question_text: Which one is malachite from the following?
questions.solution_text: Malachite is CuCO3·Cu(OH)2 (green coloured ore of copper). CuFeS2 is chalcopyrite, Fe3O4 is magnetite.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Order of basicity in aqueous solution
questions.question_text: The correct order of the basic strength of methyl substituted amines in aqueous solution is:
questions.solution_text: In aqueous solution, solvation effect (H-bonding with water) stabilizes conjugate acid. 2° amine (CH3)2NH is most basic because inductive effect (electron donation) and solvation balance optimally. Order: (CH3)2NH > CH3NH2 > (CH3)3N.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The Earth Summit held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992 was called:

options.text: to reduce CO2 emissions and global warming
for conservation of biodiversity and sustainable utilization of its benefits
to assess threat posed to native species by invasive weed species
for immediate steps to discontinue use of CFCs that were damaging the ozone layer

questions.solution_text: Earth Summit (Rio Summit, 1992) called upon all nations to take appropriate measures for conservation of biodiversity and sustainable utilisation of its benefits.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Colostrum, the yellowish fluid secreted by mother during the initial days of lactation is very essential to impart immunity to the new born infants because it contains:
questions.solution_text: Colostrum, the yellowish fluid secreted by the mother during initial days of lactation is very essential to impart immunity to the new born infant because it contains Immunoglobulin A (IgA). It imparts naturally acquired passive immunity to the newborn.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Grass leaves curl inwards during very dry weather. Select the most appropriate reason from the following:

options.text: Shrinkage of air spaces in spongy mesophyll

questions.solution_text: Bulliform (motor) cells become flaccid due to water loss during dry weather, causing the grass leaf to curl inward, reducing the exposed surface area and minimising water loss.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The shorter and longer arms of a submetacentric chromosome are referred to as:
questions.solution_text: In a submetacentric chromosome, the shorter arm is designated as 'p' arm (p = petite, i.e., short) and the longer arm is designated as 'q' arm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Respiratory Quotient (RQ) value of tripalmitin is:
questions.solution_text: $2C_{51}H_{98}O_6 + 145O_2 \to 102CO_2 + 98H_2O$. $RQ = \frac{CO_2 \text{ released}}{O_2 \text{ consumed}} = \frac{102}{145} \approx 0.7$. Fats always have RQ < 1.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a commercial blood cholesterol lowering agent?
questions.solution_text: Statins are obtained from Monascus purpureus (a yeast/fungus). They competitively inhibit the enzyme HMG-CoA reductase responsible for cholesterol synthesis, thus lowering blood cholesterol.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Match the following structures with their respective location: (a) Crypts of Lieberkühn (b) Glisson's Capsule (c) Islets of Langerhans (d) Brunner's Glands with (i) Pancreas (ii) Duodenum (iii) Small intestine (iv) Liver
questions.solution_text: Crypts of Lieberkühn: small intestine. Glisson's Capsule: liver. Islets of Langerhans: pancreas. Brunner's glands: duodenum (submucosa).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most important cause for animals and plants being driven to extinction?
questions.solution_text: Habitat loss and fragmentation is the single most important cause driving animals and plants to extinction globally (e.g., loss of tropical rainforests).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which part of the brain is responsible for thermoregulation?
questions.solution_text: Hypothalamus is the thermoregulatory centre of our brain. It is responsible for maintaining constant body temperature.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Consider following features: (a) Organ system level of organisation (b) Bilateral symmetry (c) True coelomates with segmentation of body. Select the correct option of animal groups which possess all the above characteristics:
questions.solution_text: True segmentation is present in Annelida, Arthropoda and Chordata. They also have organ system level of organisation, bilateral symmetry and are true coelomates. Mollusca lacks true segmentation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Select the correct sequence of organs in the alimentary canal of cockroach starting from mouth:

options.text: Pharynx → Oesophagus → Crop → Gizzard → Ileum → Colon → Rectum
Pharynx → Oesophagus → Gizzard → Crop → Ileum → Colon → Rectum
Pharynx → Oesophagus → Gizzard → Ileum → Crop → Colon → Rectum
Pharynx → Oesophagus → Ileum → Crop → Gizzard → Colon → Rectum

questions.solution_text: The correct sequence of organs in the alimentary canal of cockroach starting from mouth is: Pharynx → Oesophagus → Crop → Gizzard → Ileum → Colon → Rectum.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs of gases is mainly responsible for greenhouse effect?
questions.solution_text: CO2 (60%) and CH4 (20%) are the major contributors to the greenhouse effect. Other contributors include CFCs (14%) and N2O (6%).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following muscular disorders is inherited?
questions.solution_text: Muscular dystrophy is a progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle mostly due to genetic disorder. Tetany is muscular spasm due to low calcium in body fluid. Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder leading to paralysis of skeletal muscles. Botulism is a dangerous food poisoning caused by Clostridium botulinum.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The ciliated epithelial cells are required to move particles or mucus in a specific direction. In humans, these cells are mainly present in:
questions.solution_text: Bronchioles and Fallopian tubes are lined with ciliated epithelium to move particles or mucus in a specific direction. Cilia in bronchioles move mucus upward; cilia in fallopian tubes move the ovum toward the uterus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Waves of ECG and their significance
questions.question_text: Match Column-I with Column-II: (a) P-wave (b) QRS complex (c) T-wave (d) Reduction in the size of T-wave with (i) Depolarisation of ventricles (ii) Repolarisation of ventricles (iii) Coronary ischemia (iv) Depolarisation of atria (v) Repolarisation of atria. Select the correct option:
questions.solution_text: In ECG: P-wave represents depolarisation of atria. QRS complex represents depolarisation of ventricles. T-wave represents repolarisation of ventricles (return from excited to normal state). Reduction in size of T-wave indicates insufficient oxygen supply (coronary ischaemia).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a method of in situ conservation of biodiversity?
questions.solution_text: Botanical Garden is an ex situ conservation method (off-site, in human-managed system). Biosphere Reserves, Wildlife Sanctuaries, and Sacred Groves are all in situ conservation methods.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a species, newborn weight ranges from 2 to 5 kg. 97% of newborns with average weight 3–3.3 kg survive, whereas 99% with weight 2–2.5 kg or 4.5–5 kg die. Which type of selection is taking place?
questions.solution_text: Stabilizing selection favours intermediate phenotypes (average weight 3–3.3 kg) while eliminating extreme phenotypes (very low or very high weight). This reduces variation and maintains the mean.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Phases of cell cycle in order
questions.question_text: The correct sequence of phases of cell cycle is:
questions.solution_text: The correct sequence of phases is: G1 (gap 1/growth) → S (DNA synthesis) → G2 (gap 2/preparation) → M (mitosis/cell division).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: How does steroid hormone influence the cellular activities?

options.text: Changing the permeability of the cell membrane
Binding to DNA and forming a gene-hormone complex
Activating cyclic AMP located on the cell membrane
Using aquaporin channels as second messenger

questions.solution_text: Steroid hormones are lipid-soluble and directly enter the cell. They bind with intracellular receptors in the nucleus to form a hormone-receptor complex. This complex then interacts with the genome (DNA) to regulate gene expression.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.text: The hydrolytic enzymes of lysosomes are active under acidic pH
Lysosomes are formed by the process of packaging in the endoplasmic reticulum

questions.solution_text: Lysosomes bud off from the trans face of Golgi bodies, not directly from the endoplasmic reticulum. Lysosomal enzymes are synthesized by RER and processed in Golgi bodies before packaging.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Fate of floral parts after fertilization
questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements regarding post-fertilization development in flowering plants is incorrect?
questions.solution_text: Ovules develop into seeds (not embryo sac). Embryo sac is present before fertilization. After fertilization: ovule → seed, ovary → fruit, zygote → embryo, central cell → endosperm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Concanavalin A is:
questions.solution_text: Concanavalin A is a lectin (a type of secondary metabolite). It has the property of agglutinating RBCs and is used as a mitogen in immunology research.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Equipment for large scale enzyme production
questions.question_text: Which one of the following equipments is essentially required for growing microbes on a large scale, for industrial production of enzymes?
questions.solution_text: Bioreactors (fermenters) are used for large-scale production of enzymes. They provide optimal conditions (temperature, pH, O2, nutrients) for microbial growth at industrial scale.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Consider: (A) Coenzyme or metal ion tightly bound to enzyme protein is called prosthetic group. (B) A complete catalytic active enzyme with its bound prosthetic group is called apoenzyme. Select the correct option.
questions.solution_text: (A) is true: tightly bound cofactor = prosthetic group. (B) is false: enzyme protein without cofactor = apoenzyme. Complete functional enzyme (apoenzyme + prosthetic group) = holoenzyme.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Purines found both in DNA and RNA are:
questions.solution_text: Purines (double-ring nitrogenous bases) found in both DNA and RNA are Adenine and Guanine. Thymine is a pyrimidine found only in DNA; Uracil replaces it in RNA.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Path of sperm in male reproductive system
questions.question_text: Select the correct sequence for transport of sperm cells in male reproductive system:

options.text: Testis → Epididymis → Vasa efferentia → Rete testis → Inguinal canal → Urethra
Seminiferous tubules → Rete testis → Vasa efferentia → Epididymis → Vas deferens → Ejaculatory duct → Urethra → Urethral meatus
Seminiferous tubules → Vasa efferentia → Epididymis → Inguinal canal → Urethra
Testis → Epididymis → Vasa efferentia → Vas deferens → Ejaculatory duct → Inguinal canal → Urethra → Urethral meatus

questions.solution_text: The correct sequence for transport of sperm cells in male reproductive system is: Seminiferous tubules → Rete testis → Vasa efferentia → Epididymis → Vas deferens → Ejaculatory duct → Urethra → Urethral meatus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Match the hominids with their correct brain size: (a) Homo habilis (b) Homo neanderthalensis (c) Homo erectus (d) Homo sapiens with (i) 900 cc (ii) 1350 cc (iii) 650-800 cc (iv) 1400 cc. Select the correct option:
questions.solution_text: Brain sizes of hominids: Homo habilis — 650-800 cc. Homo neanderthalensis — 1400 cc. Homo erectus — 900 cc. Homo sapiens — 1350 cc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Variations caused by mutation, as proposed by Hugo de Vries, are:
questions.solution_text: According to Hugo de Vries, mutations are random and directionless (not goal-oriented). He proposed saltation (large single-step mutations) as the basis of speciation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs of organelles does not contain DNA?
questions.solution_text: Lysosomes and Vacuoles do not contain DNA. Mitochondria and Chloroplasts contain their own circular DNA (semi-autonomous organelles).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Due to increasing air-borne allergens and pollutants, many people in urban areas are suffering from respiratory disorder causing wheezing due to:

options.text: Benign growth on mucous lining of nasal cavity
Proliferation of fibrous tissues and damage of the alveolar walls
Reduction in the secretion of surfactants by pneumocytes

questions.solution_text: Asthma is a difficulty in breathing causing wheezing due to inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles. It can be due to increasing airborne allergens and pollutants and is an allergic condition common in urban areas.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Select the incorrect statement:

options.text: In male grasshoppers 50% of sperms have no sex-chromosome
In domesticated fowls, sex of progeny depends on the type of sperm rather than egg
Human males have one of their sex-chromosome much shorter than the other

questions.solution_text: In birds (including domesticated fowls), female heterogamety is found (ZW female, ZZ male). Therefore, sex of progeny depends on the type of egg produced by the female (Z-bearing or W-bearing), not the type of sperm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: DNA precipitation out of a mixture of biomolecules can be achieved by treatment with:
questions.solution_text: Chilled ethanol is used to precipitate DNA from a mixture of biomolecules during DNA isolation. DNA is insoluble in cold ethanol and precipitates as visible threads.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Select the correct group of biocontrol agents:

options.text: Bacillus thuringiensis, Tobacco mosaic virus, Aphids

questions.solution_text: Trichoderma (fungus), Baculoviruses (NPV), and Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) are used as biocontrol agents. TMV is a pathogen, aphids are pests, and others (Rhizobium, Nostoc) are biofertilizers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.ncert_chapter_name: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.question_text: Select the incorrect statement:

options.text: Inbreeding is essential to evolve pure-lines in any animal
Inbreeding selects harmful recessive genes that reduce fertility and productivity
Inbreeding helps in accumulation of superior genes and elimination of undesirable genes

questions.solution_text: Inbreeding exposes (not selects) harmful recessive genes, which are then eliminated by selection. Close and continued inbreeding may reduce fertility and productivity (inbreeding depression), but the process exposes not selects harmful recessive genes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Match: (a) Lactobacillus (b) Saccharomyces cerevisiae (c) Aspergillus niger (d) Acetobacter aceti with (i) Cheese (ii) Curd (iii) Citric Acid (iv) Bread (v) Acetic Acid
questions.solution_text: Lactobacillus → curd. Saccharomyces cerevisiae → bread (and beer). Aspergillus niger → citric acid. Acetobacter aceti → acetic acid (vinegar).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Direction of sugar transport in phloem
questions.question_text: What is the direction of movement of sugars in phloem?
questions.solution_text: Movement of sugar in phloem is bi-directional (both upward and downward) as it depends on source-sink relationship. The source sends sugar to sink regardless of direction.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In some plants, the female gamete develops into embryo without fertilization. This phenomenon is known as:
questions.solution_text: Parthenogenesis is the development of female gamete into embryo without fertilization. Parthenocarpy is development of fruit without fertilization.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Persistent nucellus in the seed is known as:
questions.solution_text: Perisperm is the persistent nucellus remaining in the seed. e.g., Black pepper, Beet. It provides nutrition to the developing embryo.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: What map unit (Centimorgan) is adopted in the construction of genetic maps?

options.text: A unit of distance between two expressed genes representing 10% cross over
A unit of distance between two expressed genes representing 100% cross over
A unit of distance between genes on chromosomes, representing 1% cross over
A unit of distance between genes on chromosomes, representing 50% cross over

questions.solution_text: 1 Centimorgan (cM) = 1 map unit = 1% recombination frequency between two genes on the same chromosome.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Heart rate calculation from cardiac output
questions.question_text: What would be the heart rate of a person if the cardiac output is 5 L, blood volume in the ventricles at the end of diastole is 100 mL and at the end of ventricular systole is 50 mL?
questions.solution_text: Stroke volume = EDV - ESV = 100 - 50 = 50 mL. Cardiac output = Stroke volume × Heart rate. 5000 mL = 50 mL × Heart rate. Heart rate = 100 beats per minute.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Thiobacillus is a group of bacteria helpful in carrying out:
questions.solution_text: Thiobacillus denitrificans carries out denitrification — conversion of nitrates/nitrites back to free N2 gas, completing the nitrogen cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Counter current mechanism and concentrated urine
questions.question_text: Which of the following factors is responsible for the formation of concentrated urine?

options.text: Maintaining hyperosmolarity towards inner medullary interstitium in the kidneys
Secretion of erythropoietin by Juxtaglomerular complex

questions.solution_text: The proximity between the loop of Henle and vasa recta, along with counter current flow in them, helps in maintaining an increasing osmolarity towards the inner medullary interstitium. This concentration gradient in medullary interstitium enables formation of concentrated urine — nearly four times more concentrated than the initial filtrate.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding mitochondria is incorrect?

options.text: Outer membrane is permeable to monomers of carbohydrates, fats and proteins
Enzymes of electron transport are embedded in outer membrane
Inner membrane is convoluted with infoldings
Mitochondrial matrix contains single circular DNA molecule and ribosomes

questions.solution_text: Enzymes of electron transport chain (ETC) are embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane (not outer membrane). The outer membrane is permeable; inner membrane is the site of ETC and ATP synthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Xylem translocates:

options.text: Water, mineral salts and some organic nitrogen only
Water, mineral salts, some organic nitrogen and hormones

questions.solution_text: Xylem translocates water, mineral salts, some organic nitrogen (amino acids from roots) and hormones (e.g., cytokinins) upward from roots to shoot.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Cells in G0 phase:
questions.solution_text: Cells in G0 phase exit the cell cycle and remain in a quiescent (non-dividing) state. They can re-enter the cell cycle if stimulated (e.g., by growth factors).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the statements given below is not true about formation of Annual Rings in trees?

options.text: Annual ring is a combination of spring wood and autumn wood produced in a year
Differential activity of cambium causes light and dark bands of tissue early and late wood respectively
Activity of cambium depends upon variation in climate
Annual rings are not prominent in trees of temperate region

questions.solution_text: Annual rings ARE prominent in temperate regions (distinct seasons cause differential cambium activity). In tropical regions, uniform climate means annual rings are less distinct or absent.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Inverted biomass pyramid in aquatic ecosystem
questions.question_text: Which of the following ecological pyramids is generally inverted?

options.text: Pyramid of biomass in a forest
Pyramid of biomass in a sea

questions.solution_text: In aquatic ecosystems (sea), the pyramid of biomass is inverted because phytoplankton (producers) have high turnover rate but low standing biomass at any time, while zooplankton biomass can exceed phytoplankton biomass.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Placentation in which ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or in peripheral part is:
questions.solution_text: In parietal placentation, ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or on peripheral regions. e.g., Mustard, Argemone. Ovary is unilocular with false septa.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following protocols aimed for reducing emission of chlorofluorocarbons into the atmosphere?
questions.solution_text: Montreal Protocol (1987) is an international treaty aimed at reducing substances that deplete the ozone layer, particularly CFCs. Kyoto Protocol deals with greenhouse gas emissions.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following contraceptive methods do involve a role of hormone?
questions.solution_text: Lactational amenorrhea involves prolactin (suppresses ovulation). Pills contain progestogens/oestrogen. Emergency contraceptives use progestogen/combinations. All three involve hormones. Barrier methods and CuT are mechanical/chemical.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Tidal Volume and Expiratory Reserve Volume of an athlete is 500 mL and 1000 mL, respectively. What will be his Expiratory Capacity if the Residual Volume is 1200 mL?
questions.solution_text: Expiratory Capacity = Tidal Volume + Expiratory Reserve Volume = 500 + 1000 = 1500 mL. (Residual Volume is not part of expiratory capacity.)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Fate of male gametes in double fertilization
questions.question_text: What is the fate of the male gametes discharged in the synergid?

options.text: One fuses with egg, other(s) degenerate(s) in the synergid
One fuses with the egg, other(s) fuse(s) with synergid nucleus
One fuses with the egg and other fuses with central cell nuclei

questions.solution_text: In double fertilization: one male gamete fuses with egg cell (syngamy) to form zygote (2n), and the other male gamete fuses with the secondary nucleus of central cell to form primary endosperm nucleus (3n).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: What is the site of perception of photoperiod necessary for induction of flowering in plants?
questions.solution_text: The photoperiodic stimulus for flowering induction is perceived by leaves (via phytochrome). The signal is then transmitted to the shoot apex where flowers are induced.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Select the correctly written scientific name of Mango which was first described by Carolus Linnaeus:
questions.solution_text: Scientific name should include genus (Mangifera) + species (indica) both in italics, with species in lowercase, and author's abbreviated name. Correct: Mangifera indica Linn. (author abbreviation after the species name).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Following statements describe the characteristics of Restriction Endonuclease. Identify the incorrect statement:

options.text: The enzyme cuts DNA molecule at identified position within the DNA
The enzyme binds DNA at specific sites and cuts only one of the two strands
The enzyme cuts the sugar-phosphate backbone at specific sites on each strand
The enzyme recognizes a specific palindromic nucleotide sequence in the DNA

questions.solution_text: Restriction endonucleases cut BOTH strands of the double-stranded DNA (not just one strand). They recognize palindromic sequences and cut the sugar-phosphate backbone of both strands at specific points.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Retention of female gametophyte in evolution
questions.question_text: From evolutionary point of view, retention of the female gametophyte with developing young embryo on the parent sporophyte for some time, is first observed in:
questions.solution_text: In Pteridophytes, the megaspore is retained within the megasporangium and the female gametophyte develops inside. This is a precursor to seed habit, first observed in pteridophytes. Gymnosperms have permanent retention (true seed habit).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In Antirrhinum (Snapdragon), red flower × white flower gave pink F1. When pink selfed, F2 showed white, red and pink. Choose the incorrect statement:

options.text: This experiment does not follow the Principle of Dominance
Pink colour in F1 is due to incomplete dominance
Ratio of F2 is 1/4 Red : 2/4 Pink : 1/4 White
Law of Segregation does not apply in this experiment

questions.solution_text: Law of Segregation is universally applicable and does apply in this cross. The experiment only violates Law of Dominance (incomplete dominance). Statements 1, 2, and 3 are correct.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: First step of glycolysis catalyzed by hexokinase
questions.question_text: Conversion of glucose to glucose-6-phosphate, the first irreversible reaction of glycolysis, is catalyzed by:
questions.solution_text: Hexokinase (in liver: glucokinase) catalyzes the first and irreversible step of glycolysis: Glucose + ATP → Glucose-6-phosphate + ADP. This phosphorylation traps glucose inside the cell.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Drug called 'Heroin' is synthesized by:
questions.solution_text: Heroin (smack) is chemically diacetylmorphine, synthesized by acetylation of morphine. It is a depressant of CNS and highly addictive.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Select the hormone-releasing Intra-Uterine Devices:
questions.solution_text: Progestasert (releases progesterone) and LNG-20 (releases levonorgestrel) are hormone-releasing IUDs. Lippes Loop and Multiload 375 are non-medicated IUDs. Vaults are barrier methods.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Allele frequency and genotype frequency calculation
questions.question_text: A gene locus has two alleles A, a. If frequency of dominant allele A is 0.4, what will be frequency of homozygous dominant, heterozygous and homozygous recessive individuals?

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is true for Golden rice?

options.text: It is Vitamin A enriched, with a gene from daffodil
It is pest resistant, with a gene from Bacillus thuringiensis
It is drought tolerant, developed using Agrobacterium vector
It has yellow grains, because of a gene from a primitive variety of rice

questions.solution_text: Golden rice is genetically engineered to produce β-carotene (provitamin A). The gene responsible was introduced from daffodil (Narcissus pseudonarcissus). It is rich in carotenoids giving it a golden colour.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Pinus seed cannot germinate and establish without fungal association. This is because:

options.text: it has obligate association with mycorrhizae
it has very hard seed coat
its seeds contain inhibitors that prevent germination

questions.solution_text: Pinus has an obligate (necessary) association with mycorrhizal fungi. The fungus increases water and mineral absorption for the plant, and in return gets food. Without this symbiosis, Pinus cannot germinate and establish successfully.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following features of genetic code does allow bacteria to produce human insulin by recombinant DNA technology?
questions.solution_text: Because the genetic code is nearly universal (same codons code for same amino acids in all organisms), bacteria can read and translate human insulin gene inserted by recombinant DNA technology.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following sexually transmitted diseases is not completely curable?
questions.solution_text: Genital herpes (caused by Herpes Simplex Virus type 2) has no complete cure. Other incurable STIs include HIV and Hepatitis-B. Gonorrhoea and Chlamydiasis are bacterial and treatable with antibiotics.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.text: Infective constituent in viruses is the protein coat
Prions consist of abnormally folded proteins

questions.solution_text: The infective constituent in viruses is the nucleic acid (DNA or RNA), not the protein coat. The protein coat (capsid) provides protection and aids in host cell recognition.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Match: (a) Pila (b) Bombyx (c) Pleurobrachia (d) Taenia with (i) Flame cells (ii) Comb plates (iii) Radula (iv) Malpighian tubules
questions.solution_text: Pila (mollusc): radula for feeding. Bombyx (arthropod/silkworm): Malpighian tubules for excretion. Pleurobrachia (ctenophore): comb plates for locomotion. Taenia (platyhelminthes/tapeworm): flame cells for osmoregulation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) refers to:
questions.solution_text: ESTs are DNA sequences corresponding to genes that are expressed as mRNA. They are partial sequences of cDNA (complementary DNA made from mRNA) and are used in gene discovery and Human Genome Project.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which is of the following statements is incorrect?

options.text: Morels and truffles are edible delicacies
Claviceps is a source of many alkaloids and LSD
Conidia are produced exogenously and ascospores endogenously
Yeasts have filamentous bodies with long thread-like hyphae

questions.solution_text: Yeasts are unicellular fungi and do NOT have filamentous bodies or hyphae. They reproduce by budding. Filamentous hyphae are characteristic of moulds and other multicellular fungi.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Match modes of nutrition in fungi
questions.question_text: Match Column-I with Column-II: (a) Saprophyte (b) Parasite (c) Lichens (d) Mycorrhiza with (i) Symbiotic association of fungi with plant roots (ii) Decomposition of dead organic materials (iii) Living on living plants or animals (iv) Symbiotic association of algae and fungi
questions.solution_text: Saprophyte: decompose dead organic matter. Parasite: live on/in living organisms. Lichens: symbiosis of algae + fungi. Mycorrhiza: symbiosis of fungi + plant roots.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following glucose transporters is insulin-dependent?
questions.solution_text: GLUT-IV is insulin-dependent and is responsible for the majority of glucose transport into muscle and adipose cells when insulin is present. GLUT-I is insulin-independent and widely distributed.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following immune responses is responsible for rejection of kidney graft?
questions.solution_text: Cell-mediated immunity (CMI), involving cytotoxic T-lymphocytes (CTLs), is responsible for graft rejection. The body recognizes foreign MHC antigens on the graft and mounts a CMI response against it.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Use of an artificial kidney during hemodialysis may result in: (a) Nitrogenous waste build-up (b) Non-elimination of excess potassium ions (c) Reduced absorption of calcium ions from GI tract (d) Reduced RBC production. Which is the most appropriate?
questions.solution_text: (a) and (b) are incorrect — dialysis does remove urea and excess potassium. (c) is correct — phosphate loss during dialysis leads to reduced Ca absorption. (d) is correct — reduced erythropoietin due to kidney disease leads to reduced RBC production.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct about cornea?

options.text: Cornea is an external, transparent and protective proteinacious covering of the eye-ball
Cornea consists of dense connective tissue of elastin and can repair itself
Cornea is convex, transparent layer which is highly vascularised
Cornea consists of dense matrix of collagen and is the most sensitive portion of the eye

questions.solution_text: Cornea consists of dense collagen matrix and corneal epithelium. It is the most sensitive part of the eye and is avascular (no blood vessels), which helps maintain transparency.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The frequency of recombination between gene pairs on the same chromosome as a measure of the distance between genes was explained by:
questions.solution_text: Alfred Sturtevant (Morgan's student) first explained chromosomal mapping using recombination frequency as a measure of distance between genes. He created the first genetic map of Drosophila.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Genes and products of lac operon
questions.question_text: Match genes of lac operon: (a) i gene (b) z gene (c) a gene (d) y gene with (i) β-galactosidase (ii) Permease (iii) Repressor (iv) Transacetylase
questions.solution_text: In lac operon: i gene → repressor protein. z gene → β-galactosidase. y gene → permease. a gene → transacetylase.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which combination of hormones can be applied to artificially induce flowering in pineapple plants throughout the year to increase yield?
questions.solution_text: Auxin and Ethylene are used to artificially induce flowering in pineapple. Auxin induces flowering directly, while ethylene helps synchronize flowering and fruit set to increase yield.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Identify the cells whose secretion protects the lining of gastro-intestinal tract from various enzymes:
questions.solution_text: Goblet cells secrete mucus (and bicarbonates) which protects the gastric and intestinal lining from digestive enzymes and concentrated HCl, preventing self-digestion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Trichoderma as biocontrol for plant disease
questions.question_text: Which of the following can be used as a biocontrol agent in the treatment of plant disease?
questions.solution_text: Trichoderma is a free-living fungus used as a biological control agent against various plant pathogens (especially soil-borne fungal diseases). It produces antibiotic substances that inhibit pathogen growth.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Phloem in gymnosperms lacks:

options.text: Both sieve tubes and companion cells

questions.solution_text: Phloem of gymnosperms lacks both sieve tubes and companion cells. Instead, gymnosperms have sieve cells (more primitive) and albuminous cells (analogous to companion cells).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Extrusion of second polar body from egg nucleus occurs:

options.text: after entry of sperm but before fertilization
before entry of sperm into ovum

questions.solution_text: Entry of sperm into the secondary oocyte triggers completion of meiosis II. The second polar body is extruded after sperm entry but before the actual fusion of nuclei (fertilization). The sperm entry breaks down MPF and activates APC.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Under which of the following conditions will there be no change in the reading frame of 5'-AACAGCGGUGCUAUU-3'?

options.text: Insertion of A and G at 4th and 5th positions respectively
Deletion of GGU from 7th, 8th and 9th positions

questions.solution_text: Deletion of 3 nucleotides (GGU = one complete codon) from positions 7, 8, 9 removes one codon without shifting the reading frame. Single insertions/deletions or 2-nucleotide changes cause frameshift mutations.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The concept of 'Omnis cellula-e cellula' regarding cell division was first proposed by:
questions.solution_text: 'Omnis cellula-e cellula' (every cell arises from a pre-existing cell) was proposed by Rudolf Virchow in 1855. This concept was fundamental to cell theory and understanding of cell division.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: What triggers activation of protoxin to active Bt toxin of Bacillus thuringiensis in boll worm?
questions.solution_text: Bt protoxin crystals are ingested by the insect. The alkaline pH of the insect gut solubilizes the crystals and activates the protoxin into active Bt toxin. The toxin then binds to midgut epithelial cells causing cell lysis and death.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Causative agent and test for typhoid
questions.question_text: Identify the correct pair representing the causative agent of typhoid fever and the confirmatory test for typhoid:
questions.solution_text: Typhoid fever is caused by Salmonella typhi. The Widal test (based on antigen-antibody reaction) is the confirmatory diagnostic test for typhoid.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: What is the genetic disorder in which an individual has an overall masculine development, gynaecomastia, and is sterile?
questions.solution_text: Klinefelter's syndrome (47, XXY) is characterized by overall masculine development, gynaecomastia (breast development in males), small testes, and sterility due to trisomy of sex chromosomes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Polyblend, a fine powder of recycled modified plastic, has proved to be a good material for:
questions.solution_text: Polyblend (recycled modified plastic waste powder) is mixed with bitumen and used for road construction. Roads made with polyblend bitumen are more durable and resistant to water seeping through.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following methods is the most suitable for disposal of nuclear waste?

options.text: Bury the waste under Antarctic ice-cover
Dump the waste within rocks under deep ocean
Bury the waste within rocks deep below the Earth's surface

questions.solution_text: Nuclear waste should be stored in suitably shielded containers and buried within rocks deep below the Earth's surface (about 500 m deep) for safe long-term disposal.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Match: (a) Insulin (b) Thyroxin (c) Corticoids (d) Growth Hormone with (i) Addison's disease (ii) Diabetes insipidus (iii) Acromegaly (iv) Goitre (v) Diabetes mellitus
questions.solution_text: Insulin deficiency → diabetes mellitus. Thyroxin imbalance → goitre. Corticoid deficiency → Addison's disease. GH hypersecretion in adults → acromegaly.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.subtopic: Types of ribs - vertebrosternal, vertebrochondral, vertebral
questions.question_text: Select the correct option regarding ribs:

options.text: 8th, 9th and 10th pairs of ribs articulate directly with the sternum
11th and 12th pairs of ribs are connected to the sternum with hyaline cartilage
Each rib is a flat thin bone and all ribs are connected dorsally to thoracic vertebrae and ventrally to sternum
There are seven pairs of vertebrosternal, three pairs of vertebrochondral and two pairs of vertebral ribs

questions.solution_text: Ribs: 7 pairs of true ribs (vertebrosternal, 1–7) connected directly to sternum via hyaline cartilage. 3 pairs of false ribs (vertebrochondral, 8–10) connected via 7th rib cartilage. 2 pairs of floating ribs (vertebral, 11–12) not ventrally connected.
